what_happened.line: The Council on Aging director reported the 41A property tax deferral program has disappeared from the town website's exemptions listing, weeks before the override vote.
The board urged seniors to attend the upcoming special town meeting and discussed what an override would mean for residents on fixed incomes.
Members voted to have a board member and a resident explore next steps and funding for a donated playground and parking-lot redesign.
The board voted to set case-by-case criteria for honorary Council on Aging membership, then voted to award one to Pete Lincoln.
The board decided to get the 41A deferral program corrected on the town website and produce handout material ahead of the override vote.

why_it_matters: The 41A deferral lets eligible seniors put off paying part of their property tax bill, and its disappearance from the town's own listing could leave residents facing a higher override bill unaware the option exists.
Seniors on fixed incomes are the group most exposed to an override's effect on the tax bill, which is why the board is pressing attendance at the special town meeting where the override is decided.

The playground and parking-lot redesign draws on funds already set aside at a prior town meeting, so its progress depends on a design estimate and possible added grant funding, not a new appropriation.
